skill.name: wp-block-development
skill.description: Develop and maintain WordPress Gutenberg blocks with guidance for metadata, registration, rendering, serialization, migrations, debugging, tooling, and testing.
skill.summary: Build reliable WordPress blocks and preserve compatibility across metadata, rendering, and saved content changes.
skill.author: Automattic

content.value_statement: WordPress block changes can break registration, saved content, or editor behavior. This skill guides implementation, migration, debugging, and verification for Gutenberg blocks.
actual_capabilities: Locates block metadata files with a bounded, read-only Node.js scanner.
Guides block.json metadata and apiVersion updates.
Explains static, dynamic, and interactive block models.
Supports attribute serialization and deprecated-version migrations.
Guides PHP metadata registration and wrapper attributes.
Provides debugging, build, lint, and testing checklists.
limitations: Targets WordPress 6.9 or later and PHP 7.2.24 or later.
Requires an existing repository path and block requirements.
Some verification workflows require Node.js, WP-CLI, or wp-env.
Does not replace browser testing or WordPress compatibility testing.

use_cases.title: Create a New Block
use_cases.description: Scaffold a block, define metadata, choose a rendering model, and verify editor and frontend behavior.

use_cases.title: Repair Invalid Content
use_cases.description: Trace serialization mismatches, attribute problems, and missing deprecations that produce invalid block warnings.

use_cases.title: Modernize Block Architecture
use_cases.description: Move existing blocks toward apiVersion 3, metadata registration, modern scripts, and compatible migrations.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Block
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the block in [path]. Explain its metadata, registration, rendering model, attributes, and required verification steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of an existing block

prompt_templates.title: Create a Block
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a [static or dynamic] WordPress block named [namespace/name] in [path] for WordPress [version]. Include tests and verification.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Invalid Content
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose the invalid block warning in [path]. Compare current saved markup with prior behavior and propose a compatible migration.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Block Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Modernize blocks under [path] for WordPress [version]. Assess apiVersion, registration, rendering, assets, deprecations, translations, and automated test coverage.

output_examples.input: Review the testimonial block before adding a rating attribute.
output_examples.output: The review identifies where attributes are stored, checks saved markup compatibility, and recommends a migration plus save-and-reload verification.

output_examples.input: Plan a dynamic event listing block.
output: Use metadata-based PHP registration and server rendering.
Keep saved content minimal and apply standard wrapper attributes.
Verify editor previews, frontend output, assets, escaping, and tests.

output_examples.input: Find why a block is missing from the inserter.
output_examples.output: The diagnosis checks the block name, metadata validity, server registration, build output, and editor console before proposing focused changes.

best_practices: Confirm the repository, block path, and supported WordPress versions before editing.
Keep block names and serialized markup stable, or add explicit deprecations and migrations.
Run repository build, lint, tests, insertion, save, reload, and frontend checks.
anti_patterns: Do not change saved markup without preserving old versions.
Do not register metadata differently between JavaScript and PHP.
Do not assume editor success proves correct frontend rendering.

faq.question: Can this skill create new WordPress blocks?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends create-block scaffolding, then guides metadata, registration, implementation, and verification.

faq.question: Does it support dynamic blocks?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers metadata-based PHP registration, server rendering, minimal saved content, and wrapper attributes.

faq.question: Can it fix invalid block warnings?
faq.answer: It helps compare serialization behavior, identify attribute issues, and add deprecated versions or migrations.

faq.question: Which WordPress versions does it target?
faq.answer: The provided guidance targets WordPress 6.9 or later and emphasizes apiVersion 3.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: It follows repository tooling and recommends build, lint, unit, end-to-end, and manual checks when available.

faq.question: What does the included scanner read?
faq.answer: It scans the current directory for block.json files and prints selected block metadata without modifying files.
